 : J U D G M E N T :

The PSI of Yeshwanthapura Police station has filed chargesheet against accused for the offence punishable u/s.498A of IPC.
 2.

The brief facts of the case of the prosecution are that the accused got acquainted with the CW 1 since 45 years and by saying that he was unmarried, he asked the CW 1 to love him and roamed with her for several times and accordingly accused took a room for rent at No.40/1,
S.C.road, Bazar street were staying there as husband and wife.
Further the CW 1 gave all her money earned in Kuwait to the accused.
That on 21/10/2017 the marriage of accused  3 CC.No.652/19 and CW 1 took place in the said room as per Muslim Customs and the accused looked after the CW 1 for about 1 month.

Thereafter, when the CW 1 came to know that the accused has already married, when she questioned the accused, he mentally and physically tortured CW1 for petty matters and also abused her in filthy language and has treated CW1 with cruelty insisting her to give Divorce and thereby committed the offences u/s.498A of IPC.
 3.
On the basis of the complaint of the CW 1, this crime has been registered by Yeshwanthapura Police Station.
After investigation, Investigating officer has submitted the chargesheet.
The cognizance for the said offence is taken.
Thereafter, on issuance of summons, the accused has appeared before the court through his counsel and filed the bail application.
Accordingly, he has released on bail.
4. The copies of the prosecution papers have furnished to the accused as contemplated u/s.207 of Cr.P.C.,

After being heard the arguments before charge, as there were no grounds to discharge him, charge for the offences u/s.498A of IPC have been framed & read over, explained to the accused in the language best known to him.
The accused has not pleaded guilty and claims to be tried.
Hence, the case taken up for trial.
5. In order to prove the guilt of the accused person, the prosecution has examined 2 witnesses as PW 1 and 2 out of 7 witnesses as cited in the chargesheet.
2 documents have been marked as Ex.P.1 and 2 .

After prosecution evidence,

6. Heard the arguments of learned APP and counsel for accused.
Perused.

7. On the basis of the above, the following points have arises for my consideration : 
 1) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that the marriage of  CW 1 with accused was solemnized on  21/10/17 as per Muslim customs and it  was a love marriage and prior to that  accused got married another girl and  when it was questioned by CW 1,
 accused mentally and physically  tortured CW1 for petty matters also  abused her in filthy language and has  treated CW1 with cruelty insisting her  to give Divorce and thereby the Accused  have committed an offence punishable  U/s.498(A) of IPC ?
 2) What order?
 5 CC.No.652/19  8.
According to the prosecution, accused has committed an offences u/s.498A of IPC.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined the brother of the complainant as PW 1 and he has deposed that the complainant is his sister and he know the accused.
Now the CW 1 is at Kuwait.

About 10 yrs ago, when CW 1 went to Kuwait, she got acquainted with accused and converted to Muslim religion and when they came to Bengaluru got married in a hotel, he and his mother have went to participate in the marriage.
Later on it brought to the notice of his sister that the accused has already got married and accused has asked her sister to give Divorce and he has told 3 times Talak Talak and Talak over the phone.
Hence, she frustrated and gone to Kuwait and also tried to commit suicide.

Thus, the PW 1 has deposed about marriage of CW 1, but not deposed The State Of Karnataka Through vs Shafiq Ahamad on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161927854/
3 about allegation of dowry harassment of accused.

sentences.text:
Hence,
learned Sr.APP has treated him as partly hostile witness and suggested that after the marriage, the accused started to ask the complainant to give Divorce and he used to assault and  6 CC.No.652/19 abuse and caused mental and physical cruelty to CW 1 and ousted away her from the house and given the statement as per Ex.P.2.
But he has denied all the suggestions of Sr.APP about mental and physical cruelty.

Since the PW 1 being the brother of the complainant has not at all deposed any kind of dowry harassment or physical or mental harassment of the accused to the CW 1, naturally doubt would accrued in the mind of the court about the case of the prosecution.
10. The prosecution further examined the mother of the complainant as PW 2 and she has deposed that the CW 1 is her daughter, she know the accused and now she is staying at Kuwaith.
About 15 years ago, the accused and CW 1 got acquainted with each other and they stayed in a hotel at Bengaluru and in her presence, the accused got married her daughter.
After marriage initially they were happy and later on the accused has sent her daughter to Kuwait.
Later on the accused has called her daughter over phone and told her that the marriage matter has brought to the notice of the family members and told 3 times Talak over phone.
Since the accused has subjected her daughter to cruelty, she tried to commit suicide by taking medicine.
But the residents have rescued her by getting admit in the hospital.

Later on her daughter came to the India and approached the accused, but by putting threat he has sent back her to parental house,
 7 CC.No.652/19 hence, she has lodged the complaint.
Thus, PW 2 being the mother has deposed about matrimonial relationship of the complainant and accused and asking to give divorce as well as saying 3 times Talak.
She has not deposed about mental and physical cruelty as alleged against the accused.

Hence,
Sr.APP has treated this witness as partly hostile witness and suggested about the case of the prosecution as well as mental and physical cruelty of the accused, but she has denied the same.

Hence, absolutely there is no material allegation to believe the alleged offence u/s.498A of IPC.
 11.

Apart from the oral evidence , Ex.P.1 is the Statement of PW 1 and Ex.P.2 is the Statement of PW 2.
 12.

On meticulous verification of the entire evidence placed by the prosecution, PW 1 and 2 being the brother and mother of the complainant have not deposed about the mental and physical cruelty caused by the accused to the CW The State Of Karnataka Through vs Shafiq Ahamad on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161927854/
4 1.

sentences.text: Hence, their evidence is not acceptable to believe the guilt of the accused.

It is significant to note here that in order to secure the presence of victim CW 1 and CW 4, 5, 6 this court has issued the summons, NBW including the proclamation, but Investigating officer has failed to execute the same and keep present them before the court.
Inspite of  8 CC.No.652/19 proclamation has been published against CW 1, 4 and 5, their presence could not be secured.

Hence, with no option CW 1,
4,5 and 6 have dropped with a liberty to the prosecution to produce the witnesses at any time without filing any recall application.
Inspite of that the prosecution has not make use of the opportunity and examined the other material witnesses.
Hence, it is a fatal to the case of the prosecution.

Similarly in order to secure the material witnesses CW 6 & 7, this court issued number of summons, NBW and proclamation, but Investigating officer has failed to execute the same and keep present them before the court.
Hence, with no option CW 6 and 7 have dropped with a liberty to the prosecution to produce the witnesses at any time without filing any recall application.
Accordingly, at the outset the prosecution is unable to get the presence of the complainant who lodged the complaint against the accused and failed to examine her.
Hence, the evidence of of CW 1 is not available.
Hence, non examination of the material witness is fatal to the case of the prosecution.
Accordingly the evidence placed by the prosecution are not sufficient to accept the guilt of the accused.
Hence, naturally the strong doubt would accrued in the mind of the court.
In a criminal justice system, if a tiny doubt arises in the mind of the court, benefit of doubt shall be extended to the accused.
In this case, not only tiny doubt but  9 CC.No.652/19 the strong doubt arise in the mind of the court, because the victims themselves have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Hence, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, in my opinion it is a fit case to extend benefit of doubt to the accused.
Accordingly point under reference answered in the Negative.

13. POINT NO.2 :
 For the aforesaid reason and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable U/s.498A of IPC.
